title: Offsets
subtitle: Monotonically increasing sequence numbers tracking consumer progress and delivery semantics.
keyTakeaways: An offset is a 64-bit integer assigned sequentially to each message within a partition, serving as its immutable logical address.
Consumer committed offsets are stored durably inside Kafka's internal compacted topic named `__consumer_offsets`.
Enabling automatic offset commits (`enable.auto.commit = true`) can cause data loss if the consumer commits offsets before asynchronous worker processing finishes.
architectureDiagram:
OFFSET ADVANCEMENT & CONSUMER POSITION
Partition 0: [ Offset 0 ][ Offset 1 ][ Offset 2 ][ Offset 3 ][ Offset 4 ][ Offset 5 ]
                                              ^                       ^
                                              |                       |
                                    Committed Offset (3)      Log End Offset (5)
                                    (Last verified in DB)     (Latest record produced)
                                    <----------------------->
                                     Consumer Lag = 2 messages

sections.heading: Offset Tracking and Internal Storage Mechanics
sections.body: Unlike traditional message brokers where the broker maintains queues of unacknowledged messages in RAM, Kafka consumers track their own reading position. A consumer maintains two offset pointers: the Current Offset (the message currently being read) and the Committed Offset (the highest message successfully processed and acknowledged).
bullets: The `__consumer_offsets` Topic: Committed offsets are written to an internal compacted Kafka topic. The key is `[group_id, topic, partition]` and the value is the committed offset integer.

Log Compaction for Offsets: Because only the latest committed offset matters, the `__consumer_offsets` topic retains only the most recent offset record per group/partition, keeping storage footprint tiny.

codeSnippet.title: Manual Offset Commit After Successful Database Transaction

sections.heading: Delivery Semantics and the Auto-Commit Hazard
sections.body: The timing of offset commits dictates whether your consumer operates with At-Least-Once or At-Most-Once semantics.
bullets: The Auto-Commit Trap (`enable.auto.commit = true`): By default, Kafka clients commit offsets automatically every 5 seconds. If a consumer fetches 100 messages, auto-commits the offset at second 5, and crashes while processing message 10, the remaining 90 messages are permanently lost on restart because the broker thinks they were committed (At-Most-Once).

Manual Commit After Work (At-Least-Once): Commit offsets manually only after the database transaction or business side effect succeeds. If the consumer crashes mid-job, the uncommitted message will be redelivered upon restart.

Reset Policy (`auto.offset.reset`): When a new consumer group starts with no committed offset, `earliest` reads the topic from offset 0 (full historical replay), while `latest` reads only messages produced after the consumer connects.

tradeOffs.pros: Guarantees zero message loss; ensures exact correlation between database persistence and offset acknowledgment.
tradeOffs.cons: Blocks consumer thread on every batch commit, reducing maximum processing throughput.
tradeOffs.bestFor: Financial transactions, payment settlements, and audit log processing.

tradeOffs.pros: Highest consumption throughput; zero manual offset tracking code.
tradeOffs.cons: Prone to silent message loss if consumers crash or throw unhandled exceptions during processing.
tradeOffs.bestFor: High-volume telemetry metrics, clickstream ingestion, and logging aggregators.

interviewTip: Never leave auto-commit enabled in a critical system design: 'We disable `enable.auto.commit` and commit offsets manually only after our database transaction succeeds. If the worker crashes mid-processing, the message will be redelivered upon restart, guaranteeing at-least-once delivery.'
